name: Leber Hereditary Optic Neuropathy

criteria.description: Presence of one of the primary mitochondrial DNA mutations (m.11778G>A, m.3460G>A, m.14484T>C)
Acute or subacute painless central vision loss in one or both eyes
Optic nerve atrophy or pallor observed on fundoscopic examination
Family history of maternal inheritance of optic neuropathy
Central or cecocentral scotomas on visual field testing

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a primary mitochondrial DNA mutation plus acute or subacute central vision loss with optic nerve atrophy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis; clinical presentation may vary.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Painless acute or subacute central vision loss
Bilateral optic nerve pallor or atrophy

common.symptomName: Visual acuity reduction to 20/200 or worse

rare.symptomName: Optic disc swelling in acute phase

laboratory: Detection of primary mitochondrial DNA mutations (m.11778G>A, m.3460G>A, m.14484T>C) via genetic testing
imaging: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing retinal nerve fiber layer thinning
MRI brain usually normal but may show optic nerve changes
genetic: Mitochondrial DNA point mutations in MT-ND1, MT-ND4, or MT-ND6 genes
other: Visual evoked potentials (VEP) showing delayed latency
Fundoscopy revealing optic nerve pallor or atrophy

distinguishingFeatures: Associated with demyelinating disease (e.g. multiple sclerosis)
History of malnutrition or vitamin deficiency

redFlags: Rapid bilateral central vision loss without pain
Family history of maternal inheritance of vision loss
Presence of primary mitochondrial DNA mutations
references: Newman NJ. Leber Hereditary Optic Neuropathy. GeneReviews® [Internet]. 2020.
Yu-Wai-Man P, et al. Leber hereditary optic neuropathy: clinical features, diagnosis, and management. Eye (Lond). 2011.
Carelli V, et al. Leber hereditary optic neuropathy: mitochondrial mutations and clinical features. Expert Rev Mol Med. 2004.
